description: Apply when you write, change, or keep a test. Assert what the code's users can observe, so that the test fails when that behavior breaks and keeps passing when only the internals change.
readme_snippet: Test Behavior, Not Implementation A test is a claim about what the code does for its users: a caller, an end user, or another service. Behavior is what those users can observe through the interface they use. That includes return values, errors, state they can read back, and effects on systems outside the code, such as a request sent, a row written, or a message emitted. Implementation is what they cannot observe: private helpers, internal call order, intermediate data, and which internal collaborator did the work. Judge each test against two imagined edits: Break the behavior. Make the code return a wrong value, skip an effect, or do the effect twice. If the test still passes, it proves nothing. The usual causes are an assertion looser than the contract, an expected value computed by the code under test, a restated constant or prompt string that never runs the code that reads it, and an assertion on data that the test built itself. Change the internals.

Modern JS has excellent browser support. Check youmightnotneedjquery.com before adding a library. YAML Structure Unit tests live in a .yml file next to the model. Top-level key is unittests:, NOT inside models:. Rules: given lists every ref() the model uses.
